newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai-Lao bridge project wins approval.
newsitem.headline: New Thai-Lao bridge project wins approval.

text.p: Thailand and Laos will build a second bridge over the stretch of the mighty Mekong river that separates their two countries, Deputy Thai Foreign Minister Pitak Intaravitayanant said on Wednesday.
The new bridge will be a gateway to Laos' Highway Nine, which stretches east to the central Vietnam seaport of Danang.
Pitak said the Thai committee for economic development and cooperation with neighbouring countries approved the $50 million project on Wednesday.
Construction of the 1.4-km (nearly one mile) bridge, to link Mudahan of north eastern Thailand with Suvannakhet in southern Laos, would start in April 1998 and take three years to complete.
He said Laos would obtain Japanese grants to meet half of the bridge's financing cost while Thailand would seek a loan to cover the rest.
The Asian Development Bank is conducting a feasibility study on a third Thai-Lao bridge linking Thasai in Laos with Chiang Khong in northern Thailand.
